nodes.name: MM Cleaning
nodes.procedure: Mo mesh (MM) was cleaned (by sonication with 1.0 M HCl, acetone, ethanol and deionized water for 30 min, respectively) and dried at 60°C in drying oven.

unit_operations.name: Sonication
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: sonication with 1.0 M HCl, acetone, ethanol and deionized water for 30 min, respectively

nodes.source_text: Firstly, Mo mesh (MM) was cleaned (by sonication with 1.0 M HCl, acetone, ethanol and deionized water for 30 min, respectively) and dried at 60°C in drying oven.

nodes.name: MoS2/MM Hydrothermal Sulfuration
nodes.procedure: MM as the substrate and sulfur powder as S source were mixed in a porcelain boat and put into the quartz tube of a tube furnace. Afterwards, the heating centre of the furnace was raised to reaction temperature of 550°C in 20 min. The furnace was held at the reaction temperature for 60 min to generate MoS2/MM, during which Ar gas was introduced with a flowing rate of 10 sccm.

nodes.name: MoS2/MM Calcination
nodes.procedure: Then the obtained MoS2/MM were calcined with Ar gas at 350°C to remove the possible excess S on the surface of MoS2/MM (named as MoS2/MM).
nodes.source_text: Then the obtained MoS2/MM were calcined with Ar gas at 350°C to remove the possible excess S

nodes.name: Electrochemical Anodic Activation
nodes.procedure: Finally, the MoS2/MM was implemented by electrochemical oxidation via cyclic voltammetry (CV) scans between +0.273 and +1.273 V vs. RHE in 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte for 1 and 8 cycles to obtain the oxygen incorporated MoS2/MM (named as O-MoS2/MM) and oxidized MoS2/MM. The scan rate of anodic oxidation experiments is 10 mV/s and the scan direction of anodic oxidation experiments is from low potential to high potential and back to low potential.

nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM image of the initial MoS₂/MM showed that the legible MoS₂ nanosheets were interconnected ... After anodic activation of 1 cycle of CV, the nanosheet morphology (Fig. 2b) ... remained basically unaltered ... after excessive anodization by 8 cycles of CVs, in Fig. 2c, most MoS₂ nanosheets disappear.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic (100) peak at 33.1° for MoS2 phase in initial and O-MoS2/MM, peak intensity significantly reduced for oxidized MoS2/MM indicating amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the XRD result in Fig. 2e, excepting for the diffraction peaks ... at 58.7° and 73.9° for Mo ... the characteristic diffraction peak at 33.1° (100) for MoS₂ was detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo 3d peaks shift +0.2 eV after 1 cycle with Mo(VI) at 232.6 eV indicating Mo-O bonds; S 2p peaks shift +0.3 eV; O 1s lattice oxygen at 530.6 eV confirms incorporation; atomic ratios 1:1.83:0 (initial), 1:1.34:0.41 (O-MoS2), 1:0.36:1.38 (oxidized).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After anodic activation with 1 cycle of CV, these two peaks positively shifted by ~0.2 eV. In addition, a small quantity of Mo(VI) 3d₅/₂ located at 232.6 eV were detected ... O 1s peak at 530.6 eV was corresponding to the binding energy of lattice oxygen ... atomic ratio Mo:S:O ... 1:1.83:0, 1:1.34:0.41 and 1:0.36:1.38.

Mo–O bonds strengthen gradually.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows ordered lattice fringes of 0.62 nm (002) and 0.27 nm (100) for initial MoS2/MM, abundant defects and disordered lattices after oxygen incorporation in O-MoS2/MM, amorphous structure for oxidized MoS2/MM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM images of initial MoS₂/MM obviously revealed the ordered lattice fringes with interplanar distances of 0.62 nm and 0.27 nm, corresponding to the (002) and (100) planes of MoS₂ ... abundant defects were observed after oxygen incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms oxygen incorporation with atomic ratios Mo:S:O = 1:2.1:0.17 (initial), 1:1.67:0.47 (O-MoS2/MM), 1:0.64:1.52 (oxidized MoS2/MM).
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS mapping further furnished incontrovertible evidence for oxygen incorporation ... The atomic ratio of Mo: S: O for initial MoS₂/MM, O-MoS₂/MM and oxidized MoS₂/MM were 1:2.1:0.17, 1:1.67:0.47 and 1:0.64:1.52.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows uniform ~6 nm thickness for initial multilayer MoS2, slightly roughened surface after 1 cycle (RMS 3.1 Å), degraded nanostructure after 8 cycles (RMS 4.7 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of initial MoS₂ on glassy carbon substrate was uniform (~6 nm) ... the RMS roughness of local region was measured as 2.7 Å, 3.1 Å and 4.7 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas are 106.7 m²/g (initial), 107.2 m²/g (O-MoS2/MM), 97.3 m²/g (repaired), mesoporosity <25 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET surface area of initial, O- and repaired MoS₂/MM was estimated to be 106.7, 107.2 and 97.3 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angles: 124.8° (initial MoS2/MM, hydrophobic), 90.0° (O-MoS2/MM), 87.5° (oxidized), 45.4° (cathodic), indicating increased hydrophilicity after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Initial MoS₂/MM possess the hydrophobic property with contact angle of 124.8° ... After the anodic ... activation, the contact angles of O-MoS₂/MM, oxidized MoS₂/MM ... were 90.0°, 87.5° and 45.4°.
